glosses: to put in order, to clean up, to tidy (up)

examples.translation: to do (clean; tidy up) the room
examples.english: to do (clean; tidy up) the room

examples.text: прибира́ть посте́ль
прибира́ть к рука́м
examples.translation: 1) to take in hand; 2) to appropriate, lay one's hands on
examples.english: 1) to take in hand; 2) to appropriate, lay one's hands on

glosses: To make an area or a thing clean; to pick up a mess; to tidy.

examples.text: Rhos station had been cleaned up for the occasion, and its single platform was gay with flags.
Mr Mayor, you were elected in a campaign to clean up the city. When are you gonna start?
At the same time, it is pouring money into cleaning up the country.
Clean up your room.

glosses: To become clean, handsome, smart in appearance, e.g. for a special occasion, especially when it is out of character to be seen as such.

examples.text: He sure cleans up nice.

glosses: To make something less corrupt or unseemly.

examples.text: clean up one's act

Gays in Providence have suggested that the raid on the Club Baths was a political action. There is some belief that the newly re-elected Cianci administration wants to prove that it is "out to clean up the city." During the election campaign, the Cianci administration was attacked by opponents as being "soft on crime."

glosses: To make a large profit; to win by a large margin, or to win a large amount, especially in gambling. Also clean house.

examples.text: Man, he sure cleaned up last night at the blackjack table.
The investors cleaned up when the stock hit the roof last year.

And for Rodgers, who cleaned up with Celtic in Scotland, this was another significant addition to his CV, as his expert guidance of Leicester - who are in a strong position to finish in the Premier League's top four and face Chelsea again at Stamford Bridge on Tuesday - now has a tangible reward in the shape of the FA Cup.

glosses: To intervene in a fight between two players at low health and easily kill both of them or the winner.

examples.text: The key here is to stop third partying and start cleaning up. Running to the first bullets you hear will only guarantee one thing, a fight. […] Cleaning up means only swooping in for the free kills. Is a fight over? Does Octane has his hands in a deathbox? That is when you take the zipline and catch them with their pants down.
She always kept her desk immaculately tidy; nothing was ever out of place.
Keep Britain tidy by picking up litter.
The scheme made a tidy profit.
Two hundred thousand people! Miss Glory, that's a tidy lot. Not bad.

glosses: In good time; at the right time; timely; seasonable; opportune; favourable; fit; suitable.

examples.text: if weather be fair and tidy

glosses: Appropriate or suitable as regards occasion, circumstances, arrangement, or order.
Normalized in a certain way that optimizes for data analysis.
A container or other device for storing or organizing loose items in a tidy fashion.

examples.text: desk tidy; sink tidy; cable tidy
It was in the days when[…]every scrap of cotton or linen found its way into the ‘tidy’.

NORRIS'S SINK TIDY. J NORRIS AND SONS, Sunningdale, near Ascot, the inventors of the "Little Friend" soap-tray, have extended the usefulness of this utensil by designing a sink-tidy for carrying three of the trays in the manner shown in the engraving. The tidy is formed by a strip of light wood[…]The price at which the tidy is offered virtually places it within the reach of everyone.
Inside there it was, the 1337 Revolving Desk Tidy.[…]The round "tidy" was divided into six segments "for all types of small sundries," and looked a bit like a grapefruit cut across the middle.

glosses: A cover, often of tatting, drawn work, or other ornamental work, for the back of a chair, the arms of a sofa, etc.

examples.text: A much coarser cotton, according to the fancy of the worker, may be used for the trimmings of night dresses, petticoats, D'Oyleys, tidies, etc.
The Tydie for her notes as delicate as they

glosses: Expression of agreement or positive acknowledgement, usually in reply to a question; great, fine.
To put (something) in its usual storage place; to place out of the way, clean up.

examples.text: Please put away the tools when you are finished.
I put the clothes away so as to neaten the room.

They burned the old gun that used to stand in the dark corner up in the garret, close to the stuffed fox that always grinned so fiercely. Perhaps the reason why he seemed in such a ghastly rage was that he did not come by his death fairly. Otherwise his pelt would not have been so perfect. And why else was he put away up there out of sight?—and so magnificent a brush as he had too.

glosses: To store, add to one's stores for later use.

examples.text: putting a little away for a rainy day
Preparing for the worst, they put away food for the winter.

glosses: To consume (food or drink), especially in large quantities.

examples.text: You wouldn't think such a small person could put away so much food.
The blonde one, old Bernice, was drinking bourbon and water. She was really putting it away, too.

glosses: To send (someone) to prison or mental asylum.

examples.text: After he was convicted, they put him away for 10 years.

It's Decoration Day.
And I knew the Hill Boys would put us away,
but my Daddy wasn't afraid.
He said "We'll fight till the last Lawson's last living day"
He put away his opponent in the first round.
When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.

glosses: To fend off, deflect; to dismiss.

examples.text: Also he told kynge Arthur that he shold mysse hym / yet had ye leuer than al your landes to haue me ageyne / A sayd the kynge / syn ye knowe of your aduenture puruey for hit / and put awey by your craftes that mysauenture / Nay said Merlyn it wylle not be / soo he departed from the kynge.
And the pharyses cam and axed hym a question: whether it were laufull for a man to putt awaye hys wyfe.

glosses: To take a large lead in a game, especially enough to guarantee victory or make the game no longer competitive.

examples.text: They put the game away by scoring three touchdowns in the fourth quarter.

glosses: To catch a fly ball or tag out a baserunner.
(pickleball) To hit the ball in such a way that the opponent cannot reach it; see passing shot
